answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns an oasis, answers a velvet, and is named by a saffron: a farm can mint saffron bindings instantly, but the oasis behind each one is disk, and the velvet will catch the ones that share it. The attacker therefore pays for real storage per head.
